summary: Follow-up on 2026-07-14 outage where Lyra saw elevated tail latency and partial request failures during a peak batch job. Meeting focused on root cause, short-term mitigations, and long-term reliability improvements including autoscale tuning, cache sizing, and failover plans.
topics: incident root cause: KV cache eviction + scale-down race
short-term mitigations: rate limiting, circuit breaker, cache warm-up
long-term: dedicated capacity, canary rollouts, runbooks
security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Carlos (Lyra SRE), Priya Rao (Lyra Head of Platform), Daniel (Lyra VP Product), Mei (Lyra Security)

00:00 - Evan: hi everyone, thanks for making time today, this is a quick followup on the postmortem we sent last week. goal is to make sure action items are clear and schedule the staging failover test
00:16 - Carlos: yeah thanks, appreciate it we had a pretty rough window on the 14th, tail latency spiked and a subset of payments went into retry loops which caused downstream duplication concerns
00:35 - Priya (SE): quick recap from our side - root cause looks like a KV cache eviction storm combined with the autoscaler cooldown which caused many replicas to scale down, then a surge re-populated causing a thundering herd and elevated p95/p99
00:50 - Mei: just to confirm, were encryption or KMS changes involved? security team saw no key errors but want to make sure nothing else was touched
01:05 - Priya Rao (customer): we didn't change keys, we did run a batch settlement job that was bigger than usual which likely bumped sequence length and cache pressure
01:25 - Evan: this matches our telemetry; we saw repeated cold KV misses and fallback to smaller model variants for some routes which increased token usage and latency, plus retries compounded load
01:50 - Daniel: can you explain "fallback to smaller model"? product team needs to know the tradeoffs because we saw degraded accuracy on some fraud checks
02:05 - Priya (SE): yes, the routing policy fell back to a compatible variant under load; it's cheaper but also less accurate for certain classification prompts — we can pin routes to avoid that during high-risk windows
02:30 - Jordan (CSM): action item: we'll recommend route pinning for payment-critical endpoints during peak settlement windows
02:45 - Carlos: short term what should we do to avoid another spike this week?
03:01 - Priya (SE): immediate mitigations: 1) tighten circuit breaker and aggressive rate limiting on batch endpoints, 2) increase autoscaler min replicas temporarily, 3) pre-warm KV cache before big jobs, 4) disable model fallbacks for payment routes
03:22 - Evan: we'll share a runnable playbook with the exact commands and RBAC notes. also adding a canary policy so changes to routing or model variants go through a small % first
03:40 - Mei: security asks: share SOC2 artifacts and confirm where audit logs for these requests are stored; we need retention info for compliance reviews
03:58 - Evan: yes, we'll attach SOC2 report and pointer to audit logs (console link). note: for Private deployments we can also provide longer retention exports to your SIEM via S3/Kinesis
04:15 - Priya Rao: long term, we want to evaluate Redwood Dedicated — predictable capacity would have avoided the scale-down shocks
04:30 - Evan: understood, we'll prepare a dedicated capacity proposal including burst settings and SLA targets, plus a canary rollout plan for the first two weeks
04:48 - Daniel: one ask from product: can we get an estimate of accuracy delta when the system falls back to the cheaper variant? we need numbers to decide whether pinning is tolerable
05:05 - Priya (SE): we'll run a focused eval with your sample prompts and give p@k and confusion matrix; that will be part of the postmortem attachment
05:28 - Carlos: i will pull the logs and KV metrics slice for the error window and upload to the ticket
05:40 - Evan: perfect, once we have those we can reproduce in staging; next step is a staged failover test where we simulate the batch job at 80-120% load and validate failovers and rate limits
05:58 - Jordan: scheduling note — we'll target the failover test for next Tuesday, priya can you confirm availability?
06:10 - Priya (SE): yes i can run it, will coordinate with Carlos on infra creds and playbook steps
06:25 - Evan: ok to recap: evan sends postmortem+runbook link, priya runs staged failover, carlos provides logs, redwood to produce dedicated capacity quote and accuracy eval, mei to confirm KMS details. any other questions?
06:45 - Mei: one more on retention: can you give an ETA on audit log export schema? we need it for our SIEM mapping
07:00 - Evan: we will include the export schema in the postmortem bundle, ETA 24-48 hours
07:12 - Daniel: thanks all, anxious to get the failover test done and avoid repeat production impact
07:25 - Evan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email and update the ticket with all artifacts and dates

Shared artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/postmortem/lyra-2026-07 (postmortem doc), https://console.redwood.example.com/logs?query=lyra-2026-07 (log link, private), slides: "Incident Overview & Mitigations" (shared deck)

End of transcript
